slides.0.title: Terroir comparisons
slides.0.subtitle: Ocean, desert, lake and Atlantic
slides.1.title: Willamette versus the Columbia Valley
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Water
slides.1.highlights.0.content: The Willamette gets about 40 inches of rain and is mostly rain-fed; Columbia Valley sites such as Horse Heaven Hills get about 6.2 inches and need irrigation
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Soils
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Willamette: basalt clay, marine sediment and loess; Columbia Valley: windblown sand and loess over gravel and basalt
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Result
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Willamette: cool, vintage-variable Pinot Noir; Columbia Valley: ripe, consistent Cabernet, Merlot and Syrah
slides.1.content: Both in the Pacific Northwest, one is rain-fed maritime and the other irrigated desert.
slides.2.title: Finger Lakes versus Long Island
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Source of moderation
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Finger Lakes: deep lakes; Long Island: the Atlantic, Long Island Sound and Peconic Bay
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Growing season
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Finger Lakes about 190–205 days; North Fork about 195–201 days
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Signature grapes
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Finger Lakes: Riesling; Long Island: Merlot, Chardonnay and Cabernet Franc
slides.2.content: Inland lakes against ocean: the first favours cool whites, the second a mild mix of reds and whites.
slides.3.title: Red Mountain versus Walla Walla
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Heat
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Red Mountain about 3,370 degree days; Walla Walla about 3,024 (from different sources, so treat as a rough comparison)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Size
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Red Mountain about 4,040 acres; Walla Walla about 182,060 acres and cross-state
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Risk
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Walla Walla winter lows can reach −20°F; Red Mountain's challenge is heat and dryness
slides.3.content: Compare terroir across four angles: heat, water, winter risk and soil.
